result_text:
`analyzeLandscape` is now a second name for `updateLandscape`, with the same options and behaviour. The module compiles offline, but I have not checked the help output: running the built jar needed an approval I couldn't get.

Changes:
- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE` and its description, which says it is the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands and the same as `updateLandscape`. It is listed in the no-argument overview next to `updateLandscape`, which stays. Both use the `getUpdateLandscapeOptions()` option set.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**: both names dispatch to the existing `updateLandscape(args)` method. Its `-help` branch prints the usage under the name the user typed (`analyzeLandscape` gets its new description, `updateLandscape` keeps its own).
- **`README.md`**: the README had no command list, so I added a short "Landscape report" section covering `analyzeLandscape`, its equivalence to `updateLandscape`, and `-help`.

Not verified: that `analyzeLandscape -help` and `updateLandscape -help` print the expected text, and that the no-argument overview shows the new entry. I also didn't run an end-to-end landscape run. `CLAUDE.md` still lists only `updateLandscape` among the main commands; I left it alone since it wasn't in scope.
